subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The trio sonata of the Baroque is usually performed by how many players?
options: Four (two melody instruments plus continuo of two players)
questions.explain: Despite its name, a trio sonata's three written parts usually require four performers because the continuo bass is realised by a chordal instrument plus a bass instrument.

questions.q: The film-scoring technique 'mickey-mousing' refers to...?
options: Using cartoon sound effects in live-action films
Improvised jazz played over the closing credits
Music that closely mirrors and synchronises with on-screen action, beat for beat
Recording the score before filming begins
questions.explain: Mickey-mousing matches the music precisely to on-screen movement, a hallmark of early animation scoring.

questions.q: A 'hook' in popular music is best described as...?
options: A modulation to the relative minor
A device for tuning the guitar
The final cadence of the song
A short, catchy musical idea designed to grab the listener and stick in the memory
questions.explain: A hook is a memorable, catchy idea engineered to capture and hold the listener's attention.

questions.q: A ritornello in a Baroque concerto is which element?
options: A recurring orchestral refrain returning between solo episodes
questions.explain: Ritornello form alternates a recurring tutti theme (ritornello) with contrasting solo episodes.

questions.q: Chopin's output is dominated by works for which instrument?
questions.explain: Chopin wrote almost exclusively for solo piano, including nocturnes, mazurkas and ballades.

questions.q: In the context of performance, 'idiomatic writing' for an instrument means...?
options: Writing only in the treble clef
Writing that ignores the instrument's natural strengths
Writing that suits the technique, range and characteristic capabilities of the instrument
questions.explain: Idiomatic writing exploits the natural technique, range and strengths of the specific instrument.

questions.q: In a major key, which chord built on the dominant typically functions as the dominant seventh?
options: A major seventh chord on the tonic
A diminished seventh chord on the leading note
A major-minor (dominant) seventh chord on scale degree 5
A minor seventh chord on the supertonic
questions.explain: The dominant seventh is a major-minor seventh chord built on the fifth degree, comprising a major triad plus a minor seventh.

questions.q: Basso continuo is most strongly associated with which period of music?
questions.explain: Basso continuo, a continuous bass with realised harmony, is a defining feature of Baroque music.

questions.q: Which key signature has four sharps?
questions.explain: E major has four sharps: F sharp, C sharp, G sharp and D sharp.

questions.q: Which woodwind instrument was a notable addition to the orchestra during the Classical-to-Romantic expansion?
questions.explain: The clarinet became a standard orchestral instrument from the late Classical period onward.

questions.q: The typical jazz 'rhythm section' that accompanies soloists usually comprises which combination?
options: Piano (or guitar), double bass and drums
questions.explain: The rhythm section conventionally consists of a chordal instrument (piano/guitar), bass and drums.

questions.q: The whole-tone scale, favoured by Debussy, divides the octave into how many equal steps?
questions.explain: The whole-tone scale consists of six pitches a whole tone apart, lacking semitones and a clear tonic.

questions.q: Which jazz style, emerging in the 1940s, is defined by fast tempos, complex chord substitutions and virtuosic improvisation, associated with Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie?
questions.explain: Bebop is the fast, harmonically complex and virtuosic jazz style pioneered by Parker and Gillespie.

questions.q: In jazz performance, 'swung' quavers are most accurately understood as pairs of quavers played roughly as...?
options: A triplet feel, long-short (approximately quarter-eighth of a triplet)
A short-long anticipation on every beat
questions.explain: Swung quavers approximate a triplet division, giving a long-short 'lilt' to each pair.

questions.q: In Indian classical music, the 'tala' refers to...?
options: The melodic ornamentation of the soloist
The cyclic rhythmic framework, a repeating cycle of beats
questions.explain: Tala is the rhythmic cycle, a repeating pattern of beats that organises the music in time.

questions.q: The 'jhalla', the closing section of a North Indian raga performance, is characterised by...?
options: A fast, exciting climax with rapid rhythmic strumming
Silence with only the drone sounding
A slow, free and unmetred mood
A return to the opening alap
questions.explain: The jhalla is the fast, rhythmically exciting climax that ends the performance.

questions.q: The Argentine 'tango' is most associated with which instrument providing its characteristic sound?
questions.explain: The bandoneón, a button accordion, gives the tango its distinctive timbre.

questions.q: In sub-Saharan African music, 'polyrhythm' refers to...?
options: The use of only one drum
A gradual slowing of the pulse
The simultaneous combination of two or more contrasting rhythms
A single rhythm played in unison by all performers
questions.explain: Polyrhythm layers two or more contrasting rhythms sounding at once, a defining feature of much African music.

questions.q: Free jazz, associated with Ornette Coleman's album 'Free Jazz' and later John Coltrane, is best described as...?
options: Big-band music with written-out arrangements only
A commercial dance style with simple harmonies
Jazz that abandons fixed chord progressions, metre and predetermined structures in favour of collective spontaneity
A return to strict ragtime forms
questions.explain: Free jazz dispenses with fixed harmony, metre and structure, prioritising collective, spontaneous improvisation.

questions.q: Which composer wrote the Brandenburg Concertos?
questions.explain: J. S. Bach composed the six Brandenburg Concertos, exemplars of the late Baroque concerto.

questions.q: The continuous sustained background pitch in Indian classical music, often provided by the tanpura, is called the...?
questions.explain: The drone is the sustained pitch (usually tonic and dominant) supplied by the tanpura beneath the melody.

questions.q: Debussy is most closely associated with which musical movement?
questions.explain: Debussy is the leading figure of musical Impressionism, using whole-tone scales and coloured harmonies.

questions.q: The technique of word-painting describes which practice?
options: Painting visual scenery for an opera
Music that reflects the literal meaning of the text
questions.explain: Word-painting depicts the meaning of the words in the music, such as rising lines on the word 'ascend'.

questions.q: A 4-3 suspension resolves by which means?
options: The third rises to the fourth
The fourth steps down to the third
The fourth leaps up to the sixth
questions.explain: In a 4-3 suspension the dissonant fourth resolves downwards by step onto the consonant third.

questions.q: The 'tabla' is...?
options: A pair of hand drums of different sizes and pitches
questions.explain: The tabla is a pair of tuned hand drums central to North Indian rhythmic accompaniment.

questions.q: Which composer is often called the 'father of the symphony' and the 'father of the string quartet'?
questions.explain: Haydn's extensive output shaped both the Classical symphony and the string quartet.

questions.q: A Neapolitan sixth chord is a major triad built on which scale degree, usually in first inversion?
questions.explain: The Neapolitan sixth is a major triad on the flattened supertonic (flattened second degree), typically used in first inversion.

questions.q: In C major, the chord built on the leading note (vii) is which quality?
questions.explain: The triad on the leading note in a major key is diminished, comprising B-D-F in C major.

questions.q: The dominant of A minor, when used to create a perfect cadence, normally contains which note as its third?
questions.explain: In the harmonic minor the leading note is raised, so E major (the dominant of A minor) contains G sharp.

questions.q: In composition, developing a musical idea through 'sequence' means...?
options: Repeating a melodic pattern at a higher or lower pitch
questions.explain: A sequence repeats a melodic or harmonic pattern at a different pitch level.
